title: He Played Circuit's Son at Six — Now Vir Hirani Leads Rajkumar Hirani's OTT Debut
excerpt: Pritam and Pedro drops July 3 on JioHotstar with Arshad Warsi and Boman Irani — plus a Sanjay Dutt cameo that Arshad accidentally let slip at the trailer launch
body:
The boy was six years old, and he wouldn't give the shot until someone paid him.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=uCjkRVV0-qU

That's how Arshad Warsi remembers Vir Hirani on the set of Lage Raho Munna Bhai two decades ago, when the kid played ShortCircuit — the tiny, mischievous son of Warsi's iconic Circuit. "Jab tak usko paise nahin diye, usne shot nahin diya!" Warsi recalled at the trailer launch in Mumbai, grinning like a man who has watched a child literally grow up and walk into his father's spotlight.

Twenty years later, that child is leading Rajkumar Hirani's most personal project to date. Pritam and Pedro, Hirani's first-ever streaming series, drops on JioHotstar on July 3 — and it carries the weight of an entire legacy on its young shoulders.

"Standing next to him as a co-actor feels truly surreal and emotional. It honestly feels like watching someone you've known as a child grow into such a sincere and talented actor." — Arshad Warsi
**"It honestly feels like watching someone you've known as a child grow into such a sincere and talented actor." — Arshad Warsi

The setup is pure Hirani, filtered through a digital-age lens."**

The setup is pure Hirani, filtered through a digital-age lens. In Goa, an abandoned ATM on a beach becomes ground zero for a cybercrime investigation that spirals into kidnapping, hacking, and the kind of warm chaos that only this filmmaker knows how to orchestrate. Vir plays Pritam Parker, a tech-savvy hacker whose moral compass keeps spinning. Warsi plays Inspector Pedro Gonsalves, a traditional cop drowning in a world where crime has gone wireless. The mismatched-pair energy is instant — and the Munna Bhai DNA is unmistakable.

!Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

But this isn't nostalgia for nostalgia's sake. Vikrant Massey turns villain as Martin, and from the trailer alone, he looks electric in the role — sharp, cold, and having far too much fun being the bad guy. Boman Irani returns to Hirani's orbit, where he arguably does his finest work, and Mona Singh fills a pivotal role the makers are keeping deliberately vague. Behind the camera, Avinash Arun — the director behind the devastating Killa and the cinematographer of Sacred Games — gives the series a visual texture that prevents it from tipping into broad comedy, even as the plot gets delightfully unhinged.

The trailer launch itself was a spectacle that Hirani clearly designed as a statement. Cyber security expert Amit Dubey — whose real-life encounters with the Mumbai Cyber Cell inspired the show during COVID lockdown — hacked a journalist's phone live on stage. And then, just when the crowd thought the surprises were over, Shreya Ghoshal walked out and performed Piya Piya Piya, a track composed by Shantanu Moitra with lyrics by Swanand Kirkire — the same duo behind Lage Raho Munna Bhai's music. The room went very quiet, then very loud.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZmTzHYsDa3/

And then Arshad Warsi did the most Arshad Warsi thing possible: he accidentally confirmed that Sanjay Dutt appears in the series. He tried to walk it back. It did not work. If true, Munna Bhai himself shows up in Hirani's streaming debut — the kind of full-circle moment that fan fiction couldn't have written better.

Hirani, for his part, was disarmingly honest about the leap. "My first film was released in December 2003," he said. "We used to worry whether people's phones might ring in the theatre. Now we filmmakers wonder if a notification will pop up and distract the viewer." It's a quietly stunning admission from someone who spent two decades perfecting the theatrical experience — and who is now betting his warmth, moral clarity, and comic instinct can survive a six-inch screen.

As for Vir's preparation: director Avinash Arun revealed that Hirani's son had been quietly reading screenplay drafts while performing a 15-minute English monologue in a stage play no one from the production had planned to attend. "The way he was holding the stage, I found it amazing," Arun said. "We realised we should consider Vir for this character. No one got the slightest idea."

The timing is almost absurdly perfect for Warsi, who now has three releases within 15 days — Welcome To The Jungle, Dhamaal 4, and now this. "Can't wait for the audience reactions to the characters I have portrayed," he said, with the calm of a man who knows exactly how good his summer is about to get.

Pritam and Pedro streams on JioHotstar from July 3 in India, the US, UK, Canada, and Australia.
